brief:
Raja Shehadeh, a Palestinian writer and lawyer, has had his personal diaries archived at an institution in Edinburgh, according to Al Jazeera. The 75-year-old described the daily documentation spanning decades as an act of resistance. Shehadeh, a leading intellectual voice, spoke about the significance of preserving his records during an interview in the Scottish capital.

The archival project safeguards Shehadeh's written observations and reflections on Palestinian life and politics. His diaries represent a firsthand historical account maintained over an extended period, offering detailed perspective on events and conditions in Palestinian society.
dek: Al Jazeera interviews the leading writer and lawyer, 75, in Edinburgh, where his daily documentation is being archived.
title: Palestinian writer Shehadeh's diaries archived in Edinburgh
